subject: Prospect Q&A — where requests run, data lineage, and export controls
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sagecardio.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: SageCardio Security <security@sagecardio.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 08:15:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Qs on where data is processed and cross-border handling

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — really useful. Our security team asked for a short Q&A so we can validate any EU-to-US movement for PII and confirm deletion guarantees. Can you cover the following briefly?

- Which geographic regions can host inference execution (specifically EU options)?
- Which third-party subprocessors are involved in the runtime path (compute, storage, telemetry)?
- How does Redwood handle cross-border transfers; do you use SCCs or other legal mechanisms?
- What does deletion look like end-to-end (request -> purge), including caches and backups?

If possible, please attach any short evidence packets or a subprocessor CSV. We can then loop in procurement for DPA language.

Appreciate it —
Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Security Programs
SageCardio

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sagecardio.com>
Cc: SageCardio Security <security@sagecardio.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 09:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where data is processed and cross-border handling

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a concise walk-through and attachments. Attaching: residency-evidence-20270930.pdf and subprocessor-inventory-20270930.csv.

1) Execution regions we support (hosted + dedicated + private):
   - US: us-east-1 (primary), us-west-2 (secondary)
   - EU: eu-west-1 (Dublin) and eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) — we can pin inference to EU-only pools for Dedicated/Private customers
   - APAC: asia-southeast-1 (Singapore) — available for region-specific deployments

2) Subprocessor categories and examples (runtime path):
   - Compute: cloud GPU hosts (AWS EC2 / GCP GPUs) in the region you select
   - Storage: object stores (S3/GCS) for model artifacts and optional customer artifact caches (encrypted at rest)
   - Networking & egress: cloud VPCs + cloud provider backbone; we do not route traffic through additional cross-border vendors by default
   - Monitoring/observability: Datadog (telemetry), Sentry (error collection) — telemetry can be disabled or routed to customer-owned endpoints on Private/Dedicated
   - Secrets/KMS: AWS KMS by default; we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Dedicated and Private deployments

3) Cross-border transfer controls / legal mechanisms:
   - For Hosted customers routing outside the EU, we offer Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs) as part of our DPA.
   - For customers requiring no cross-border transfer, Redwood provides EU-only execution by pinning workloads to EU Dedicated pools or Private deployments (no egress from that jurisdiction unless explicitly configured).
   - Fallbacks: routing policy prevents automatic failover to non-EU hosts unless you opt-in for multi-region failover for availability reasons.

4) Deletion lifecycle (high level):
   - Delete request from customer (API/Console) triggers immediate application-layer tombstoning (zero access) within 1 hour.
   - Data purge: primary storage objects are scheduled for permanent deletion and removed within 30 days for standard retention policies, 90 days for archival retention (customer-configurable).
   - In-memory caches / KV cache: ephemeral; KV caches are scrapped per session and not retained beyond configured TTL (default 5 minutes).
   - Backups & logs: backup retention varies by type; backups containing user content are purged per policy and we provide attestations on request.

Notes and options for SageCardio specifically:
   - If you need an EU-only processing commitment for PII, we recommend Dedicated (reserved EU GPU pool) or Private (VPC/on-prem). Both options support customer-managed KMS and can restrict all subprocessors to EU-region endpoints where feasible.
   - We can provide a scoped SOC2 report and a subprocessor manifest (see attached CSV).

Next steps: happy to set a short call with Marissa (solutions engineering) to review technical controls and a narrow DPA with SCCs. If that works, I can seed a DocuSign with the DPA and the SCCs clause.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sagecardio.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: SageCardio Security <security@sagecardio.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 10:30:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where data is processed and cross-border handling

Thanks Karthik — helpful. A couple quick clarifications from our security team:

- For EU-resident PII that triggers GDPR data subject requests, if we pin to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) can you confirm no staging/telemetry or third-party storage will leave the EU? We need clear affirmative language for procurement.
- For the KMS flow: if we use customer-managed keys, do you perform any key escrow or can keys be fully managed and rotated on our side?
- Can you provide the SOC2 link and a redacted subprocessor contract for legal review?

If we get those answers and a brief technical walk-through, procurement can progress the DPA with SCCs.

Appreciate the quick turnaround —
Alex

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood-inference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@sagecardio.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood-inference.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Thu, 30 Sep 2027 12:40:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Quick Qs on where data is processed and cross-border handling

Alex — short answers and proposed next steps below. Quoting your questions inline for clarity.

> if we pin to eu-central-1 (Frankfurt) can you confirm no staging/telemetry or third-party storage will leave the EU?
Yes. When you choose an EU-only Dedicated or Private deployment, all runtime compute, model artifacts, ephemeral caches, and observability endpoints can be constrained to EU regional endpoints. Our standard hosted tier may send aggregated telemetry to a US-based observability backend; we will not do that for EU-pinned deployments. We will provide procurement-ready language confirming that no subprocessors will export EU-resident PII outside the EU for the scoped systems.

> if we use customer-managed keys, do you perform any key escrow or can keys be fully managed and rotated on our side?
Customer-managed keys (CMKs) are supported and keys can remain under your control. We do not escrow your CMKs. We integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM) and access requires your key policy. Rotation and revocation are managed by your KMS.

> Can you provide the SOC2 link and a redacted subprocessor contract for legal review?
Yes — SOC2 (redacted) and the subprocessor inventory are attached and available via the secure links above. For any sensitive redactions you need, we can provide a control-mapping pack via an NDA.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical call (30 min) with Marissa (solutions engineering) this week to validate the EU-pinned configuration and audit trail options.
- We will seed a DPA with SCCs (DocuSign link below) and attach the scoped residency commitment for EU-only execution.
- Ben (copied) will coordinate procurement-specific redlines and provide a redacted subprocessor contract if legal wants it.

DocuSign draft: https://www.docusign.com/record/abc123
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8739

If that plan looks good I can have Marissa propose time slots.

Thanks —
Karthik
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
